sections.overview: The Nazca booby is an eastern Pacific seabird, now recognized as distinct from the masked booby.
sections.identification: Adults are mostly white with dark wings and tail; the orange-pink bill helps distinguish it from the yellow-billed masked booby.
sections.habitat: It forages over tropical open ocean and breeds on remote islands, including the Galápagos.
sections.diet: It is a fish-eating predator that catches prey by plunging into the sea.
sections.behavior: It spends much of its time at sea and returns to islands to breed.
sections.reproduction: It nests on open ground or cliffs on oceanic islands.
sections.ecology: The Nazca booby was formerly treated as a subspecies of the masked booby; studies support its recognition as a separate species.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern, while reporting a decreasing population trend.
